summary: A resumed PR whose branch is fix/<n>-… and whose body says Refs #<n> instead of Closes #<n> makes fsgg-coord verify-paths report SKIP, so the declared-Paths guard never runs and the out-of-scope file it would have caught stays invisible.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord verify-paths S.I.R.#252 --pr 254 -> 'FSGG-PATHS SKIP — cannot tell which issue PR #254 implements (branch is not item/<n>-…, and it closes no issue)'; issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#252 declares Paths: feedback/audits/2026-08-16-sir-item-220-bounded-pr-ci.audit.json, scripts/ci-integrity-plan.mjs, scripts/test-ci-integrity-plan.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml; PR #254 changes scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json, which is in none of them
cost: none yet; detected at resume rather than at merge, but the guard was skipped for the whole life of the PR up to head 8972d37
owner: EHotwagner/S.I.R. scripts/fsgg-coord verify-paths binding heuristic; pnext-item worker branch-naming convention

summary: The dispatch brief described PR #254 as substantively complete and needing only the v2 review ledger, and described the review-wait entry as gating the review-decision record; both are wrong, and either would have sent a lane to the review gate with a false model of the protocol.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord review 'S.I.R.#252' --pr 254 --json -> reasons:['dispatchCritic requires a durable review-wait entry before dispatch'] proves the wait entry gates CRITIC DISPATCH, not the decision record; PR #254 body states verbatim 'The second half - that a conditional integrity subject can leave the default branch red with no signal at all - is untouched and still open', contradicting the brief's 'fully green ... resume it' framing; acceptance criteria 3 and 5 of issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#252 are unimplemented at head 8972d37
cost: none incurred - caught by reading the PR body before dispatching a critic; had the brief been followed literally a fresh critic would have been dispatched against an incomplete implementation at 8972d37 and a passing review would have been recorded for an item missing two of five acceptance criteria
owner: work-board-best host dispatch-brief authoring; the brief derived completeness from the CI rollup and review markers rather than from the PR body's own scope statement

summary: Writing the gate-inversion mutants BEFORE handoff found a real hole in my own regression test: every sweep assertion was written relative to subjectOrder, so deleting feedback-audit from that list shrank the sweep silently and the whole suite still passed.
evidence: command:python3 invert.py (12 mutants over scripts/ci-integrity-plan.mjs and .github/workflows/ci.yml) -> first run 10/12 killed, survivor 'feedback-audit deleted from the subject inventory'; after adding an absolute pin (assert.deepEqual(subjectOrder, [...5 ids])) the second run reports 12/12 killed with the suite green before and after each mutation; file:scripts/test-ci-integrity-plan.mjs
cost: none - the hole was found and closed at authoring time rather than by the critic; had the mutants not been run, the regression test for an item about gates silently not running would itself have permitted a gate to silently not run
owner: EHotwagner/S.I.R. scripts/test-ci-integrity-plan.mjs; the reusable pattern is that a relative assertion over a registry list cannot detect deletion from that list, so registry-shaped invariants need one absolute pin

summary: check-invalidation --base/--head validates an append-only exception ledger as a per-diff assertion, so it errors once per ledger entry the current change set does not touch and cannot pass on any realistic diff; it is documented as the commit-time check and cited as passing Verification evidence on closed items while being structurally incapable of passing.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi .agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/scripts/feedback-tool.fsx -- check-invalidation --base origin/main --head HEAD -> 'FAIL: validation failed (15 error(s))' exit 1; file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/scripts/FeedbackReportTool.fs line 542 'if List.length matches <> 1 then errors.Add(...overbroad or mismatched...)' where the `invalidated` set holds only citations the current diff touches; measured 17 ledger entries with 17 errors at head 8972d37 and 15 errors at head 1c34852 after two entries were legitimately re-sealed, i.e. errors = entries - entries-touched-by-diff; issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#258
cost: one avoidable misdiagnosis loop: I first compared 8972d37 against my own work and read an identical 17/17, concluding my changes added nothing, when in fact my changes were still uncommitted so both runs measured the same commit; the real 17->15 signal only appeared after committing
owner: FS-GG fs-gg-feedback-report skill, FeedbackReportTool.fs invalidation checker; vendored into this repo in two mirrors (.agents and .claude) that must stay in sync, so the semantic fix belongs upstream rather than diverging the mirrors

summary: The feedback-tool checkpoint CLI is documented only as a bash invocation with double-quoted arguments, so any backtick in evidence or summary text is command-substituted by the shell and silently deleted from the recorded checkpoint; the tool accepts the mutilated text and reports success.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi feedback-tool.fsx -- checkpoint --evidence "... where the (backtick)invalidated(backtick) set holds ..." emitted "/bin/bash: line 1: invalidated: command not found" on stderr, then "feedback-tool: appended checkpoint" on stdout with exit 0; the stored JSONL line read "where  holds only citations", losing the identifier; validate-checkpoint-state --cycle item-252-audit-binding-ledger-currency then reported PASS on the corrupted content
cost: one corrupted checkpoint entry requiring manual JSONL repair; the failure is silent in the tool output and only visible as an unrelated-looking bash diagnostic interleaved above a success line
owner: FS-GG fs-gg-feedback-report skill; SKILL.md checkpoint examples should single-quote the free-text arguments, or the tool should read them from a file/stdin, since evidence text routinely contains backticked identifiers and code

summary: ReviewWait.generationToken mints a token for any round and ReviewWait.validate accepts the resulting Transition, and the board write is durable, but the round is only checked at projection time by review <ref> --pr N, so a wrong round is discovered only after two irreversible ledger writes have been made.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord review wait "S.I.R.#252" wait-body.json --pr 254 --json with reviewGeneration derived from ReviewWait.generationToken(head, Kind.InitialReview, 1) -> accepted, {"commentId":5382794822}; then command:scripts/fsgg-coord review "S.I.R.#252" --pr 254 --text -> "UNDETERMINED — the durable review wait does not authorize dispatchCritic: expected generation 1c3485223c9229c6567cd6251547918b2379e632:initial-review:0, got ...:initial-review:1"; recovery required a Cancel transition (commentId 5382797353) and a re-Enter at round 0 (commentId 5382797762); the initial review round is 0-based and no packed skill states it
cost: two avoidable durable ledger writes on PR #254 that record only a wrong guess, plus one reflection cycle over FS.GG.Coord.Core.dll to recover the WaitReceipt/Transition shapes because no packed skill documents the review wait command at all
owner: FS-GG coordination engine, FS.GG.Coord.ReviewWait: the producing function does not enforce the invariant its consumer requires; either generationToken/validate should reject a non-zero round for InitialReview, or the refusal text should be produced before the write. Subject of S.I.R.#255.

summary: Concurrently dispatched lanes are given isolated git worktrees but share one scratchpad directory, so lanes silently overwrite each other files; three of mine were replaced mid-task by sibling lanes writing the same generic filenames.
evidence: The harness scratchpad path is identical across lanes. My commit-msg.txt was replaced by lane tern-fc83 commit message for S.I.R.#256 ("Point agent sessions at the pinned .NET SDK"), and my reflect.fsx and reflect2.fsx were both replaced by another lane own reflection scripts over the same FS.GG.Coord.Core.dll while I was using them. Detected only because the harness emits a "changed on disk since you last read it" notice; a lane that wrote a file and later read it back without that notice would silently consume another lane data.
cost: none realised in this lane - my commit was already made and I did not re-read the overwritten scripts - but the exposure is real: git worktree isolation is enforced strictly while the scratchpad, which holds commit messages, PR bodies, generated event payloads and validation fixtures, is not isolated at all
owner: work-board-best host lane dispatch, or the harness scratchpad allocation: a per-lane scratchpad subdirectory keyed by worker id would remove the whole class
